reading_comprehension.q: 1. According to the passage, why can no one earn God's favour by keeping the law?
reading_comprehension.a: No one can be justified by works, because all have sinned and no one keeps the law perfectly.

reading_comprehension.q: 2. How was Abraham justified, and why does the timing matter?
reading_comprehension.a: He believed God's promise, and God counted his faith as righteousness — about 400 years before the law was given.

reading_comprehension.q: 3. What does it mean to be justified?
reading_comprehension.a: To be declared righteous by God, as if we had never sinned; it is a free gift of grace through faith in Christ.

reading_comprehension.q: 4. What four blessings does Romans 5 say belong to those who are justified by faith?
reading_comprehension.a: Peace with God, access into grace, hope of God's glory, and hope that does not put us to shame — even in suffering.

listening_questions.q: 1. According to Romans 3, why can no one be justified by works of the law?
listening_questions.a: Because all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; no one can keep the law perfectly.
To be declared righteous by God, as if you had never sinned — a gift of grace, not a wage for good works.

listening_questions.q: 3. How was Abraham justified, and when did he live in relation to the law?
listening_questions.a: By faith — he believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness. He lived about 400 years before the law was given.

listening_questions.q: 4. According to Romans 5:1-2, what do we have since we have been justified by faith?
listening_questions.a: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, and access by faith into this grace.

listening_questions.q: 5. What would happen if we were justified by works?
listening_questions.a: Grace would not be grace, and boasting would be possible. If we trusted in our own works, we would never know if we had done enough.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Pronunciation — /θ/ or /ð/?
exercises.instruction: Say each sentence aloud. Write /θ/ (voiceless — no vibration, as in faith, think, through, truth) or /ð/ (voiced — throat vibrates, as in father, this, that, with) for the key word in each sentence (the word with th). Put your fingers on your throat to feel the vibration.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Second Conditional — Form
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with the correct second conditional form: If + past simple, would + base verb. Remember: use 'were' (not 'was') after 'if' for all persons in formal English.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Second Conditional — Match the Halves
exercises.instruction: Match each If-clause (1-6) with the correct result clause (A-F).

exercises.title: Exercise 4: Vocabulary Matching
exercises.instruction: Match each word with its correct definition.

exercises.title: Exercise 5: Reading — True or False?
exercises.instruction: Read the passage in Section 5 again. Mark T (true) or F (false). Correct the false sentences.

exercises.title: Exercise 6: Translation Lab (Vietnamese to English)
exercises.instruction: Translate into natural English. Use the second conditional in sentence 1.

speaking_task: Roleplay in pairs (3 minutes): Student A is a friend who thinks we must earn God's favour by good works. Student B explains justification by faith using Romans 3-5. Use at least 3 second conditional sentences (e.g. 'If we were justified by works, grace would not be grace.') and 4 vocabulary words from Section 3. Swap roles and repeat.
writing_task: Write a short letter (80-100 words) to a friend who is afraid that God will not accept them because of their sins. Explain justification by faith from Romans 3-5. Use at least 3 second conditional sentences and 4 vocabulary words from Section 3. Begin: 'Dear friend, I want you to know that God loves you...'

written: A. Write 5 second conditional sentences about justification, using these beginnings: 1) If we were justified by works, ... 2) If Abraham had trusted in his own works, ... 3) If Christ had not died for us, ... 4) If I trusted in my own goodness, ... 5) If you believed God's promise today, ...

B. Write a short paragraph (80-100 words) explaining justification by faith to a friend. Use at least 3 second conditional sentences and 4 vocabulary words from Section 3. Begin: 'Dear friend, let me tell you the best news I have ever heard...'
homework.listening: Listen to the audio again. Fill in the missing words: 'If we were justified by _______, grace would not be _______. Abraham believed God, and it was _______ to him as righteousness. Since we have been justified by _______, we have _______ with God.' Then answer: According to the dialogue, why does the Friend now have peace?
homework.memory_verse: Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. — Romans 5:1 (ESV). Also learn Romans 4:3: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
